story.introBody: The Great Starlight Beacon has fallen asleep! Walk the paths with Pip the Owl, help the magical friends of each region, and cast learning spells to restore the kingdom's light.
story.restoredBody: You awakened the Whispering Woods, lit the Crystal Caves, restored the Enchanted Library, and crowned Starfall Tower with light!
story.endingSubtitle: Every lantern, crystal, storybook, and star in Moonwood is glowing thanks to you!
story.endingFriends: Your companions Pip, Moss, Bramble, Luma, and Astra dance beneath the restored constellations.

map.heading: Choose a quest

pip.name: Pip the Owl
pip.greeting: Hoo-hoo! Tap any glowing path or ask me whenever you want a helpful clue!

moss.name: Moss the Forest Sprite

bramble.name: Bramble the Crystal Mole

luma.name: Luma the Librarian Fox
luma.greeting: Every plank on the bridge and every word in our storybooks holds a wonderful secret!

astra.name: Astra the Starlight Sprite
astra.greeting: Look up at the stars! Shapes, logic puzzles, and workshops show how the constellations dance!

forestGate.title: The Whispering Gate

mossGrove.title: The Heartwood Tree

crystalCaves.title: Crystal Caves
crystalCaves.intro: Pack crystals into rune bags of ten.

echoForge.title: The Echo Minecart

prismSanctum.title: The Prism Vault

ravineBridge.title: The Ravine Bridge

enchantedLibrary.title: The Enchanted Library

livingStorybook.title: The Living Storybook

sigilTemple.title: Sigil Temple

starObservatory.title: The Starlight Astrolabe

1.passage: Pip the owl carried a small brass lantern to the wooden bridge so Moss could see the stepping stones.
1.prompt: Why did Pip carry the brass lantern to the bridge?
1.label: So Moss could see the stepping stones

2.passage: Bramble sorted his shiny purple gems into neat bags of ten before locking the cave vault.
2.prompt: Who sorted the shiny gems into bags of ten?
2.label: Bramble the crystal mole

3.passage: First, Luma dusted the book cover. Next, she opened the golden clasp. Last, she read the star poem.
3.prompt: What did Luma do right after dusting the book cover?
3.label: She opened the golden clasp

4.passage: First, Aria planted a tiny seed in soil. Next, she watered it each morning. Soon, a green sprout popped up.
4.prompt: What happened first in Aria's garden story?
4.label: Aria planted a tiny seed in soil

5.passage: Because a sudden rainstorm wet the wooden planks, the ravine bridge became slippery and Luma waited inside.
5.prompt: Why did Luma wait inside instead of crossing the bridge?
5.label: The rain made the bridge planks slippery

6.passage: The tower bell was silent because a sleepy squirrel had tucked pinecones inside the bell's rim.
6.prompt: What caused the tower bell to stay silent?
6.label: Pinecones were tucked inside the bell

7.passage: Astra put on her warm wool cloak,lit the hearth fire, and watched white flakes drift past the tower window.
7.prompt: What season is it most likely in Astra's story?
7.label: A snowy winter evening

8.passage: Moss packed a watering can, a trowel, and a packet of sunflower seeds before walking to the sunny clearing.
8.prompt: What will Moss most likely do next at the sunny clearing?
8.label: Plant and water the sunflower seeds

parent.confidenceHeading: How Mastery & Assessments Work (And What This Game Cannot Determine)
parent.confidenceBody: Provisional mastery requires at least 5 independent unseen successes (85% accuracy hypothesis) across 3+ task families and 2+ representations, without Hint 3 answer revelation. Retained mastery requires delayed review and transfer checks. These are game-based curriculum indicators—not clinical assessments, IQ scores, or school grade rankings.
parent.recommendationsHeading: Recommended Offline Activities for Grown-Ups & Children

recommendReason.needsSupport: Suggested because recent attempts used hints or showed a specific misconception:
recommendReason.practicing: Suggested to build fluency on a skill currently in practice:
recommendReason.nextSkill: Suggested as a great next foundational step:

offline.addWithin20: Combine two small groups of household objects (spoons, coins, or blocks) up to 20 and practice 'making a ten' first.
offline.subtractWithin20: Start with 12–15 small counters, hide a few under a cup, and ask your child how addition helps figure out how many are hidden.
offline.unknownEquations: Play 'Mystery Cup': show 10 buttons in all, put 6 on the table, and ask '6 plus how many in the cup makes 10?'
offline.tensAndOnes: Bundle 10 toothpicks or crayons with a rubber band to show 1 ten, then build numbers like 34 and compare with 43.
offline.compareLengths: Pick 3 household items (a pencil, spoon, and book), order them shortest to longest, and measure them end-to-end with paperclips (no gaps!).
offline.composeShapes: Cut paper squares and triangles to build larger hexagons or towers, and fold a paper circle into 2 equal halves and 4 equal quarters.
offline.phonicsWords: Write letter tiles on index cards (s, a, t, m, p, f, r, o, g) and practice sliding sounds smoothly together without adding 'uh'.
offline.starPatterns: Count steps out loud by 2s, 5s, and 10s while walking or climbing stairs together.
offline.readingComprehension: After reading a short picture book together, ask 'What happened first, next, and last?' and 'Why did the character do that?'
offline.vocabularyOral: Pick a descriptive word from today's story (like 'sturdy' or 'fragile') and take turns finding 3 things in the room that fit.
offline.spellingWriting: Invite your child to write a 1-sentence note or label a drawing on paper, checking for a capital letter at the start and a period at the end.
offline.logicalReasoning: Play 'I Spy with Clues' ('It is not round, and it is not blue...') and ask your child to explain how they ruled out choices.
offline.scienceNature: Go on a 5-minute nature walk to compare a living plant (needs water, air, sunlight) with a nonliving pebble.
offline.creativeConstruction: Give your child 10 blocks or cups to build a bridge that spans between two books and ask why their design stays up.
